reader.requirement: At --std 85, when the qualified set of rule 1 identifies several objects for a name referenced in contained program B, at most one may be local to B (two locals are an ambiguity); B's own declaration is the referenced object, otherwise the object of A if A declares it (globally), otherwise that of the nearest further container that declares it, for data-names, condition-names, file-names, record-names and report-names, across name classes (a nearer condition-name hides a farther data-name and vice versa).

reader.notes: SymbolTable.NearestDeclaring narrows a qualified multi-candidate set to the minimum containment depth (0 = B, 1 = A, 2.. = further containers) and leaves a plural same-tier set ambiguous; the cross-class hides (NearerConditionNameHides, NearerDataNameHides, ReportScope.NearerEntryHides) apply 3a across name classes. Every lettered arm probed at 85 conforms; the path never consults the edition.

refuter.evidence: Rule 3a: 'If the name is declared in program B, the object in program B is the referenced object', and §1985:X.1.3.8 applies it across classes ('even when it is a different type of user-defined word'). The reader probed condition-name against data-name only. Probes at --std 85: r4a_local_file_hides_global_data and r4d_local_file_hides_global_data_witness: B declares FD FX, the container 01 FX GLOBAL; B's MOVE 'LOCL' TO FX writes the container's FX (OUT BEFORE FX=GLOB / OUT AFTER FX=LOCL) instead of naming B's file (which must make the MOVE invalid). r4b_local_data_hides_global_file: B declares 01 GX, the container FD GX GLOBAL; B's OPEN OUTPUT GX opens the container's file (exit 0, IN GX=DATA) instead of naming B's data item. r4c_local_data_hides_global_cond (data vs condition, the arm the code has): IF CC refused COBOL2318, correct. At --std 2023 r4d and r4b behave identically (cause b). Code: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/SymbolTable.cs#NearestDeclaringData lines 124-132 test only ReportScope.NearerEntryHides and NearerConditionNameHides; the file-name lookup (DataBindState#VisibleFiles via InheritedGlobals) has no nearer-data-name test. cite.py: OK §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR3a; OK §1985:X.1.3.8. kb/Work: none found; PB4219 (landed) fixed the same ranking only for APPLY COMMIT / I-O-CONTROL operands. Sibling to sweep: an own index-name or own report-name against a container's global data-name or file-name.
refuter.corrected: NONCONFORMING (under-rejects, wrong-answer): 3a is not applied between file-names and data-names. Minimal program r4d_local_file_hides_global_data_witness.cob: expected a refusal of MOVE ... TO FX in B (B's FX is a file); observed OUT AFTER FX=LOCL (the container's GLOBAL data item overwritten). Cause b: the same at --std 2023.

adjudication.reason: A contained program's own file-name does not hide its container's GLOBAL data-name of the same word (and the reverse): `MOVE "LOCL" TO FX` in the contained program, where FX is its file, changes the container's item. `§1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR3a`. I ran it. 2023 rows `GR-8.4.6.2.1-1`, `GR-8.4.6.2.1-3`.
